samples.summary: Large unrelated feature (share-link live revalidation + new public endpoint + editor handle revocation) bundled into the #1045 undo-granularity change
samples.evidence: The originating task doc `docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md` states Goal: "One user action = one undo unit for every selection-replacing edit" and its Plan covers only `withUndoUnit`, the batching call sites and the Yorkie undo floor. This diff also adds a brand-new public backend route (`POST /share-links/resolve`), rewrites `SharedDocumentByToken` from `useState/useEffect` to a 60 s react-query refetch, adds `revocableDocStore` + `EditorAPI.isDisposed()/dispose()` neutering, `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` / `YorkieNoteStore.dispose()`, and `readOnly` remount deps in three views — none of which is an undo-unit concern and none of which has its own task doc under `docs/tasks/active/`. The share-link work is a coherent feature in its own right (it even gets its own `docs/design/sharing.md` section), which is the point: it should have been its own change so it could be reviewed and reverted independently of the undo fix.

samples.summary: New public endpoint `POST /share-links/resolve` not recorded in the canonical backend REST reference
samples.evidence: `docs/design/backend.md` is the repo's endpoint-by-endpoint backend reference and still lists only `GET /share-links/:token/resolve` (lines 323–327, including its 404/410 semantics). The new POST form — which is now the only route the frontend calls — is documented only in `docs/design/sharing.md`. Per CONTRIBUTING's design-doc discipline the canonical subsystem doc for backend routes should carry it (or at least cross-reference), otherwise the two docs give different answers about what the API surface is. The enforced backticked-path check does not catch omissions.

samples.summary: Two live routes now answer the same question with no removal plan recorded
samples.evidence: `POST /share-links/resolve` is added while `GET /share-links/:token/resolve` is kept "for the one-shot callers that already exist (an older frontend served during a rollout)". After this change no in-repo client calls the GET form (`packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts` posts; the CLI never resolves share tokens) — only `authenticated-http.e2e-spec.ts` and the log-redaction spec exercise it. A rollout-compat duplicate is reasonable, but neither the controller comment, `docs/design/sharing.md` nor the task doc records when/by whom the token-in-path route is removed, so the repo is left permanently maintaining two resolve surfaces (and two redaction rules).

samples.summary: The undo-unit batching rule is now written into three duplicate copies of indent/outdent/toggleList instead of a shared helper
samples.evidence: `indent`/`outdent`/`toggleList` exist in `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts` (3676/3702/3729), `text-editor.ts` (2821/2845/2773) and `text-box-editor.ts` (1148/1171/1104), each with its own `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`/`INDENT_STEP` and now each with its own `doc.batch(...)` / `withUndoUnit(...)`. The change acknowledges this in `docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md` and defers unification to #1048, but the immediate cost is that the undo-unit rule is a four-way copy-paste invariant — and the branch already demonstrates it can drift: `TextBoxEditorAPI.applyBlockStyle` (text-box-editor.ts:1104) is the one copy that was left unbatched.

samples.summary: Same per-write data-loss class left on other multi-write mutators after the scope was widened to close it
samples.evidence: Round 13 widened this change specifically because "Tab is one undo unit but the Increase-indent button is a hundred" shipped the same data loss behind a different control. The widening stopped short of `mergeTableCells` / `splitTableCell` (one op per cell, unbatched), `applySpellSuggestion` (two units) and `TextBoxEditorAPI.applyBlockStyle` — all listed as deliberate follow-ups in the task doc. A merge over a table with more than ~50 cells is still the pre-fix shape on `YorkieDocStore`. These are outside the issue's literal "selection-replacing edit" wording, so this is graded as an incompletely closed class rather than an unmet criterion, but the rationale used to widen scope applies to them equally.
